176:gives the general pitch; the worked examples in
177:`DescriptiveComplexity.Examples.ConjunctiveQueries` (conjunctive-query
178:evaluation and containment) and `DescriptiveComplexity.Examples.GraphCrawling`
179:(Web data acquisition, with a cardinality threshold, a reachability
180:certificate and an ordered reduction) are the hands-on tutorials;
181:individual declarations are documented on their own pages.
182:
183:## The framework: problems, interpretations, reductions
184:
185:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Interpretation` – a `DescriptiveComplexity.DecisionProblem`
186:  is an isomorphism-invariant property of finite structures of a *relational*
187:  language (invariance is baked into the notion, as is standard in descriptive
188:  complexity; so is relationality, via an `IsRelational` instance argument –
189:  the standing convention of the field, so every class equality below is a
190:  statement about relational problems). A
191:  `DescriptiveComplexity.FOInterpretation` is a tagged,
192:  `dim`-dimensional first-order interpretation of one language in another,
193:  and a `DescriptiveComplexity.FOReduction` (notation `P ≤ᶠᵒ Q`) is one that
194:  maps yes-instances exactly to yes-instances, on the *finite* nonempty
195:  structures – the only ones membership and hardness ever read. Tags replace
196:  the linear order that textbook FO reductions use to encode constantly-many
197:  sorts of elements.
198:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Composition` – the pullback of a formula through an
199:  interpretation and the composition of interpretations, giving reflexivity
200:  and transitivity of `≤ᶠᵒ` (a `Preorder` on problems, usable in `calc`).
201:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Ordered` and
202:  `DescriptiveComplexity.OrderedComposition` – reductions over the ordered
203:  expansion of the source language, `DescriptiveComplexity.OrderedFOReduction`
204:  (notation `P ≤ᶠᵒ[≤] Q`): order-invariant FO(≤) reductions, correct on every
205:  finite linearly ordered input. This is the standard notion of the field and
206:  the home of gadget constructions that genuinely need an order.
207:
208:## The abstract complexity layer
209:
210:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Complexity` – `DescriptiveComplexity.ComplexityClass`,
211:  with membership, hardness and completeness, closed by construction under
212:  (ordered) FO reductions. Membership and hardness depend only on the
213:  *finite* instances of a problem, making explicit that these statements say
214:  nothing about infinite structures.
215:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Encoding` – bringing your own instance types: a
216:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Encoding` bundles a concrete instance type, its declared
217:  size, a computable encoding into finite structures, and polynomial bounds
218:  *both ways* between size and universe – no padding, no compression – so an
219:  encoding cannot be built size-dishonest. Semantic agreement is the separate
220:  predicate `DescriptiveComplexity.Encoding.Faithful`. That the bounds have
221:  teeth is a theorem: no unary encoding of subset-sum passes them
222:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.no_unary_encoding`, in
223:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Encoding.UnaryBlowup`).
224:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Encoding.BinarySubsetSum` – the positive contrast,
225:  worked out in full and in both directions. The honest binary encoding of a
226:  list of weights and a target (`DescriptiveComplexity.binarySubsetSumEncoding`),
227:  its decoding lemmas and `DescriptiveComplexity.binarySubsetSumEncoding_faithful`
228:  make `DescriptiveComplexity.knapsack_NP_complete` a statement about concrete
229:  lists of binary-written numbers; `DescriptiveComplexity.bwDecoding` reads
230:  *hardness* back the same way, and needs no well-formedness condition, a
231:  structure whose order is not linear being a definite no-instance. Both rest
232:  on `DescriptiveComplexity.hasSubsetSum_iff_index`, which reads the problem
233:  along any injective indexing of the items, and on the
234:  `DescriptiveComplexity.selection_toIndex`/`selection_ofIndex` pair that any
235:  other problem quantifying over selections of items reuses.
236:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Decoding` – the decoding direction, for reading
237:  *hardness* concretely: well-formedness conditions as decision problems
238:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.DecisionProblem.ofSentence`, restricting a problem to
239:  its non-junk instances as `W ⊓ P` with one-line upgrades of existing
240:  completeness proofs), and computable decodings
241:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.Decoding`) from concretely presented structures back
242:  to concrete instances, with the same executable hygiene as the encoders.
243:  Both tutorials – `DescriptiveComplexity.Examples.ConjunctiveQueries` and
244:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Examples.GraphCrawling` – open with a concrete
245:  instance type and its bundled encoding, and close the loop with a decoder
246:  and a well-formed completeness theorem.
247:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Degree` – completeness *without a class*: the downward
248:  closure `DescriptiveComplexity.ComplexityClass.below Q₀` of a fixed problem
249:  under ordered FO reductions is itself a `ComplexityClass`, so
250:  `(below Q₀).Complete P` is literally “`P` is `Q₀`-complete”, with no logic
251:  anywhere – the notion behind “GI-complete”
252:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.GI`, the degree of `DescriptiveComplexity.GraphIso`).
253:  Hardness needs no new proof: `DescriptiveComplexity.CofinalHard` is already
254:  parameterized by an arbitrary membership predicate. Completeness for a degree
255:  is mutual reducibility
256:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ComplexityClass.complete_below_iff`), and the degree
257:  depends only on the degree
258:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ComplexityClass.below_congr`). The construction is
259:  checked against the classes that have complete problems, in
260:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ClassDegrees`: `NP = below SAT`,
261:  `coNP = below TAUT`, `PTIME = below HORN-SAT`, `NL = below 2SAT` and
262:  `RE = below FINSAT` (`DescriptiveComplexity.NP_eq_below_sat` and siblings),
263:  so “SAT-hardness is NP-hardness” is a lemma rather than folklore.
264:
265:## The polynomial hierarchy, defined logically
266:
267:* `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrder` (with `…Lift`, `…Pull`, `…Ordered`) –
268:  existential/universal second-order definability with `k` quantifier-block
269:  alternations.
270:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Hierarchy` – the levels `Σₖᵖ`/`Πₖᵖ` and `PH` as
271:  complexity classes, via Fagin's ([Fagin 1974][fagin1974generalized]) and
272:  Stockmeyer's ([Stockmeyer 1976][stockmeyer1976polynomial]) theorems. The
273:  level inclusions and the duality `Πₖᵖ = co-Σₖᵖ` are proved, not assumed.
274:  Level 0 is `DescriptiveComplexity.PTIME`, polynomial time, defined by the Horn
275:  fragment SO-Horn (below); the level-0 statements that would amount to
276:  closure under complement are the one thing the fragment does not give, and
277:  are restricted to levels `≥ 1`. Everything remains a definition or a
278:  theorem: the library declares **no axioms** (check with `#print axioms`).
279:
280:## Polynomial time, by the Horn fragment
281:
282:* `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrderHorn` – SO-Horn ([Grädel
283:  1992][gradel1992capturing]): existential second-order logic whose kernel is a
284:  conjunction of Horn clauses in the quantified relation variables, the
285:  fragment that captures polynomial time on ordered structures. The kernel is
286:  represented as *data* (`DescriptiveComplexity.HornProgram`, a list of clauses with a
287:  first-order guard over the ordered expansion, body atoms and an optional
288:  head), which is Grädel's clausal normal form and what a reduction consuming
289:  such a definition needs to read.
290:* `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrderHornPull` – the pullback of an SO-Horn definition
291:  through an interpretation *stays Horn*: the Horn condition constrains only
292:  the second-order atoms, and an interpretation rewrites the
293:  input-vocabulary ones, which live in the guard. This closure is what makes
294:  `DescriptiveComplexity.PTIME` (in `DescriptiveComplexity.Hierarchy`) a genuine complexity
295:  class, and hence level 0 of the hierarchy, *defined* by SO-Horn definability
296:  just as NP is defined by `Σ₁`-definability. HORN-SAT is PTIME-complete – hard
297:  by the Horn discharge, and a member by the Horn program that computes unit
298:  propagation along the order – which also yields the four inclusions of level
299:  0 into level 1, and with them the monotonicity of the hierarchy
300:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.sigmaP_mono`, `DescriptiveComplexity.piP_mono`): the padding
301:  step of `DescriptiveComplexity.Hierarchy` climbs only from level 1 up, its level-0
302:  step being the Horn discharge. See `DescriptiveComplexity.Problems.HornSat` for what
303:  is and is not claimed.
304:
305:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Difference` – **the class DP**
306:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.DP`), the conjunctions of an NP condition and a coNP one
307:  ([Papadimitriou & Yannakakis 1984][papadimitriou1984complexity]), with
308:  `NP ⊆ DP` and `coNP ⊆ DP`. Closure under reductions is the interesting part:
309:  the two halves of a DP definition are individually *not* order-invariant, so
310:  an ordered reduction cannot be pulled back half by half in the usual way. The
311:  order is instead quantified in opposite directions on the two sides –
312:  existentially on the `Σ` half, universally on the `Π` half – whose conjunction
313:  is again the pullback, each half then handled by the sentence-level order
314:  elimination of `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrderOrdered`. The upper bounds
315:  `DP ⊆ Σ₂ᵖ ∩ Π₂ᵖ` merge the two kernels into one alternation, in either block
316:  order. SAT-UNSAT, the canonical DP problem, is defined in
317:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Problems.SatUnsat` and proved DP-complete: *in* DP by
318:  projecting each of its two sides onto a plain CNF instance and inheriting
319:  definability from SAT, and DP-hard in
320:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Problems.SatUnsat.Hardness` by running the Cook–Levin
321:  discharge of the `Σ₁` half and of the complement of the `Π₁` half side by side
322:  into one paired instance.
323:
324:* `DescriptiveComplexity.FixedPoint` – FO(LFP) ([Immerman
325:  1986][immerman1986relational]; [Vardi 1982][vardi1982complexity]), in the same
326:  clausal style: a rule system defining a least fixed point, plus an
327:  *unrestricted* first-order output sentence read at it. Because the output may
328:  negate fixed-point atoms, FO(LFP) definability is closed under complement by
329:  construction (`DescriptiveComplexity.LFPDefinable.compl`) – the one thing the Horn
330:  fragment cannot do head-on – and every SO-Horn definition transports into it
331:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.SigmaSOHornDefinable.lfpDefinable`).
332:
333:* `DescriptiveComplexity.FixedPointHorn` – the converse translation, the hard half of
334:  Grädel's equivalence: every FO(LFP) definition compiles back into the Horn
335:  fragment, by deriving the *complement* of the fixed point stage by stage
336:  along the order and evaluating the output sentence clausewise
337:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.LFPDefinable.sigmaSOHornDefinable`). The two formalisms are
338:  therefore interchangeable
339:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.lfpDefinable_iff_sigmaSOHornDefinable`), which read against
340:  the definition of the class is **Immerman–Vardi**, `PTIME = FO(≤, LFP)`
341:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.lfpDefinable_iff_mem_PTIME`); SO-Horn definability
342:  is closed under complement (`DescriptiveComplexity.SigmaSOHornDefinable.compl`), and
343:  level 0 of the hierarchy collapses: `PiP 0 = SigmaP 0`
344:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.piP_zero_eq`), polynomial time closed under complement. The
345:  order-walking machinery shared with the HORN-SAT program lives in
346:  `DescriptiveComplexity.OrderWalk`.
347:
348:## The inflationary and partial fixed points
349:
350:* `DescriptiveComplexity.FixedPointStep` – **one iteration skeleton for
351:  FO(IFP) and FO(PFP)** (`DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef`): a block of relation
352:  variables, one unrestricted first-order step formula per variable, an output
353:  sentence. The two logics differ only in what a step does with the previous
354:  stage – accumulate into it or replace it – so the stages, their
355:  stabilization on finite structures (through the orbit pigeonholes of
356:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Iterate`, a file free of library concepts), their
357:  transport along isomorphisms and their pullback through an interpretation
358:  are all built once, on `DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef.next` alone.
359:* `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrderBlockHom` – **morphisms of blocks**: an
360:  arity-preserving map of relation variables induces a morphism of the
361:  blocks' vocabularies, along which sentences transport
362:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.SOBlock.realize_homSentence`) – the bookkeeping for
363:  reading a formula written for one block inside a larger block containing a
364:  copy of it, which the translations between the fixed-point logics need.
365:* `DescriptiveComplexity.FixedPointInflationary` – **FO(IFP)**
366:  ([Gurevich–Shelah 1986][gurevich1986fixed]; [Abiteboul–Vianu
367:  1989][abiteboul1989fixpoint]): iterate inflationarily, read the output at
368:  the limit. Ordered (`DescriptiveComplexity.IFPDefinable`) and order-free
369:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.IFPDefinableFree`) definability are kept apart – for
370:  the fixed-point logics, unlike for SO(TC), the two must differ or the
371:  Abiteboul–Vianu theorem would be trivial. Closed under complement by
372:  construction and under (ordered) reductions; FO(LFP) embeds by reading a
373:  rule system as one simultaneous step
374:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.LFPDefinable.ifpDefinable`), which needs no
375:  positivity because inflation supplies the monotonicity.
376:* `DescriptiveComplexity.FixedPointInflationaryLFP` – **FO(≤, IFP) = FO(LFP)**
377:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ifpDefinable_iff_lfpDefinable`), whence the capture
378:  theorem **FO(≤, IFP) = PTIME**
379:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ifpDefinable_iff_mem_PTIME`): an inflationary
380:  definition compiles back into FO(LFP) by walking the stages
381:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.FixedPointHorn`'s stage apparatus) with a *dual*
382:  positive evaluator deriving truth and falsity of the step formulas'
383:  subformulas per stage – inflation is what makes the complement of a stage
384:  advance positively, which is precisely why PFP admits no such translation
385:  and goes to SO(TC) instead. The output sentence survives unchanged modulo
386:  the block injection, which is why the target is FO(LFP) and not SO-Horn.
387:* `DescriptiveComplexity.FixedPointPartial` – **FO(PFP)** ([Abiteboul–Vianu
388:  1989][abiteboul1989fixpoint]): iterate by replacement, read the output at
389:  the first stable stage – requiring convergence, a divergence convention
390:  chosen deliberately and compared precisely with the textbook one
391:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef.realize_pfpValue_iff`). FO(IFP) is contained
392:  in it by disjoining each variable's own atom onto its step
393:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef.inflate`) – the easy inclusion of
394:  Abiteboul–Vianu, in both the ordered and the order-free form. The PSPACE
395:  capture lives with the other PSPACE files, below.
396:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Invariant.Pebble`,
397:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Invariant.EquivK`,
398:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Invariant.Stages` – **the `≡ᵏ`-invariant layer**:
399:  the `k`-pebble refinement over an abstract initial relation
400:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.EquivK`, a greatest fixed point with its coinduction
401:  principle `DescriptiveComplexity.le_equivK`, expansion lemma
402:  `DescriptiveComplexity.equivK_inf_eq` and pair-substructure closure
403:  `DescriptiveComplexity.equivK_of_pairSub`), its instantiation at agreement
404:  on the atomic type over a relational structure – relative to a family of
405:  relation symbols, since a definition only mentions finitely many
406:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef.exists_usesRels`) – the `k`-variable
407:  invariance lemma (`DescriptiveComplexity.realize_equivK` – a formula with
408:  enough room for its quantifier depth cannot separate `≡ᵏ`-equivalent
409:  tuples; no syntactic `k`-variable fragment is ever defined), and the
410:  `≡ᵏ`-invariance of every inflationary and partial stage of a `StepDef`
411:  within its variable budget
412:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef.inflLimit_invariant`,
413:  `DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef.partStage_invariant`).
414:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Invariant.OrderedPebble`,
415:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Invariant.OrderDef` – **the canonical order on
416:  `≡ᵏ`-classes**: the ordered pebble refinement, a strict order on `k`-tuples
417:  growing as the classes split, whose incomparability is stage by stage the
418:  pebble refinement (`DescriptiveComplexity.ordStage_invariant`) and at the
419:  limit `≡ᵏ` (`DescriptiveComplexity.incompRel_ordK_eq`) – a linear order on
420:  the classes, *inflationary by construction*, so computed by one relation
421:  variable of a simultaneous induction (`DescriptiveComplexity.ordStepDef`,
422:  with `DescriptiveComplexity.inflStage_ordStepDef` matching the two
423:  round for round) and canonical because inflationary stages transport along
424:  isomorphisms.
425:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Invariant.Structure`,
426:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Invariant.Simulation`,
427:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Invariant.Backward` – **the invariant structure
428:  `Iᵏ A`** (`DescriptiveComplexity.InvMap`: the `≡ᵏ`-classes of `k`-tuples,
429:  with atomic-type bits, substitution and rearrangement relations, and the
430:  linear order induced by the canonical order,
431:  `DescriptiveComplexity.invLinearOrder`) **and the two-way simulation**: the
432:  pebble compiler (`DescriptiveComplexity.pebbleCompile`) runs a `k`-variable
433:  induction over `A` on the classes –
434:  `DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef.pfpHolds_invStepDef`, every quantifier
435:  spending a pebble along a substitution relation – and the class compiler
436:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.backCompile`) runs an induction over the *ordered*
437:  invariant vocabulary back on `A`, each class variable becoming `k` element
438:  variables and the order read off the (frozen) order variable
439:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef.ifpHolds_backStepDef`).
440:* `DescriptiveComplexity.FixedPointStratify` – **stratification**: nested
441:  inflationary inductions are one induction
442:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef.ifpHolds_stratify`) – the second stratum,
443:  a `StepDef` over the base vocabulary *expanded by the first stratum's
444:  block*, is gated on an arity-`0` variable derived exactly when the first
445:  stratum's step formulas add nothing, so it replays its own stages over the
446:  frozen limit.
447:* `DescriptiveComplexity.FixedPointOrderTransfer` – **order relativization**:
448:  FO(≤, IFP)/FO(≤, PFP) definability of `P` is order-free definability of
449:  `DescriptiveComplexity.DecisionProblem.withOrder P` («the order symbol is a
450:  linear order, and `P` holds on the reduct») over the ordered expansion, and
451:  order-free definability implies ordered definability
452:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef.liftOrder`).
453:

 succeeded in 5733ms:
889:## The numeric predicates, and AC⁰
890:
891:The bottom of the ordered world, and the only vocabulary here that is a
892:*function of the order* rather than part of an instance.
893:
894:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Arithmetic` – the arithmetic expansion
895:  `FirstOrder.Language.arith`: a binary `≤` and two ternary symbols read on a
896:  finite linear order through the rank of an element
897:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.orank`), as `orank x + orank y = orank z` and
898:  `orank x * orank y = orank z`. Relations, not functions, hence *truncated*: a
899:  sum that does not fit has no witness, and overflow is the first-order
900:  `¬∃z, plus x y z` (`DescriptiveComplexity.no_plus_iff_card_le`). Since the
901:  interpretation is canonical, an FO(≤) sentence is read arithmetically by a
902:  language map (`DescriptiveComplexity.sumOrderToArith`), and – the smallest
903:  thing the numeric predicates buy over a bare order – the *size* of the
904:  universe becomes visible: `DescriptiveComplexity.evenCardSentence` says that
905:  it is even, by the parity of the top rank.
906:* `DescriptiveComplexity.ArithmeticDefinable` – **AC⁰** as a logic:
907:  `DescriptiveComplexity.AC0Definable`, one sentence over the arithmetic
908:  expansion deciding the problem on every finite ordered instance. Classically
909:  this is `FO(≤, +, ×) = FO(≤, BIT)` and (DLOGTIME-)uniform AC⁰ ([Immerman
910:  1999][immerman1999descriptive], Thm 1.17; [Barrington, Immerman & Straubing
911:  1990][barrington1990uniformity]); the vocabulary identification
912:  `FO(≤, +, ×) = FO(≤, BIT)` – both halves of Thm 1.17 – **is a theorem here**
913:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ac0Definable_iff_ltDecidable`, below), while the
914:  circuit reading stays classical, no circuit model being introduced. `+` and `×`
915:  are primitive rather than `BIT` because it is *they* whose interpreted-universe
916:  analogue is schoolbook arithmetic on base-`n` digits, where `BIT`'s is base
917:  conversion. Two features distinguish this notion from every other definability
918:  notion here: there is **no order-free variant**, the numeric predicates being
919:  meaningless without an order; and closure under complement is free
920:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.AC0Definable.compl`), the defining object being a
921:  sentence, where NL needed Immerman–Szelepcsényi. `FO(≤) ⊆ AC⁰` is transport
922:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.FODefinable.ac0Definable`) and is **strict**, by EVEN
923:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.exists_ac0Definable_not_foDefinable`, below).
924:* `DescriptiveComplexity.ArithmeticFixedPoint` – **`AC⁰ ⊆ PTIME`**
925:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ac0Definable_mem_PTIME`), because the numeric
926:  predicates are themselves an induction: two relation variables of arity 3,
927:  `plus` walking `y` and `z` down the order in lockstep and `times` peeling one
928:  copy of `x` off `y` and adding it back with `plus`, in *one simultaneous*
929:  `DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef` – no stratification, the occurrences being
930:  positive. Soundness is an induction on the stages, completeness needs no stage
931:  count at all, only that the limit is closed under the clauses
932:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.inflLimit_arith_iff` is the resulting identification of
933:  the limit with the arithmetic). What makes the last step free is that the
934:  numeric predicates are *symbols*: the translation of an AC⁰ sentence is a
935:  language map (`DescriptiveComplexity.arithToBlock`), not a recursion, and
936:  `StepDef` accepts an unrestricted first-order output – which is exactly what an
937:  AC⁰ sentence needs, its numeric atoms sitting under any number of negations.
938:  The route through `FO(DTC)` does not work in the same way: a
939:  `DescriptiveComplexity.TCSpec` is one operator over first-order kernels with no
940:  relation variables, so the sharper `AC⁰ ⊆ LOGSPACE` wants the multi-head
941:  automaton instead. `DescriptiveComplexity.HeadArith` is the beginning of that
942:  route: `DescriptiveComplexity.HeadProgram.plusP` **decides the addition of two
943:  ranks** (`DescriptiveComplexity.HeadProgram.decides_plusP`), by walking one
944:  scratch head up from the first summand while a second counts to the second
945:  summand. The design decision that makes its specification clean is that the
946:  overflow marker – needed because “this head is at the greatest element” is not
947:  a quantifier-free fact of one head, while “these two heads are equal” is – is
948:  **parked by the fragment itself**, as a third scratch head, rather than being
949:  an input the caller must have prepared: a marker sitting anywhere else gives a
950:  walk with three regimes (exit `false` early, answer, or run off the end with no
951:  exit at all), and a specification stated by the marker's value, as
952:  `DescriptiveComplexity.HeadProgram.lexRel` must be.
953:  `DescriptiveComplexity.HeadProgram.timesP` then **decides the multiplication**
954:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.HeadProgram.decides_timesP`) with an addition *inside*
955:  it: an outer loop counts the rounds, and in each round a **scan** walks a
956:  candidate up the order asking `plusP` whether it carries the accumulator plus
957:  the first factor – which is how a decider is made to compute. Its three-level
958:  head layout is what makes the composition work: interface, then the four
959:  working heads, then the addition's own scratch heads, the middle level being
960:  where `DescriptiveComplexity.HeadProgram.runs_wireP`'s locality requirement
961:  lives.
962:* `DescriptiveComplexity.HeadEvalArith` – **`AC⁰ ⊆ LOGSPACE`**
963:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ac0Definable_mem_LOGSPACE`), the sharp bound, by
964:  evaluating the sentence with a deterministic multi-head automaton of
965:  `qdepthA φ + 7` heads. It is `DescriptiveComplexity.HeadProgram.evalP` with one
966:  case split four ways: an atom of the input vocabulary and an atom of `≤` stay
967:  quantifier-free **guards**, while `plus` and `times` become the two *programs*
968:  above – they are not relations of the instance at all, but functions of the
969:  order, so they must be computed and not read. The sweep, the branch and the
970:  head accounting are reused unchanged, which is why the file is short; what it
971:  adds is `DescriptiveComplexity.relVar` and `DescriptiveComplexity.relTerm`
972:  (over a relational vocabulary a term *is* a variable, which is how an atom's
973:  arguments become head indices) and the head layout
974:  `DescriptiveComplexity.HeadProgram.ArithScratch`, seven heads above the
975:  quantifier region. With this the bottom of the ladder is pinned:
976:  `FO(≤) ⊊ AC⁰ ⊆ LOGSPACE ⊆ NL ⊆ PTIME`, the first inclusion strict and the
977:  strictness of the second exactly the switching lemma.
978:* `DescriptiveComplexity.LogTime` – **a machine model for the bottom of the
979:  ladder**, in the shape the logarithmic-time hierarchy prescribes
980:  ([Sipser 1983][sipser1983borel];
981:  [Barrington, Immerman & Straubing 1990][barrington1990uniformity]) rather than
982:  that of circuit families. A `DescriptiveComplexity.LTMachine` fills a list of
983:  registers, each by one of the two players – a register is an address of
984:  `DescriptiveComplexity.posCount A ≈ log n` bits, so filling one is the
985:  logarithmic block of guesses of the `Σₖ-TIME(log n)` normal form, and an
986:  alternation is a change of polarity along the list – and then runs a
987:  deterministic **bit-level** base: a Boolean combination of *queries* (an input
988:  relation at a tuple of registers, which is the random access to the instance:
989:  reading the input at an address *is* evaluating a relation at a tuple), of
990:  *reads* (`DescriptiveComplexity.BaseTest.bit`: the bit of one register at the
991:  position named by another, the random access to the machine's own addresses)
992:  and of *sweeps*, single passes over the bit positions by a finite automaton
993:  reading one bit of each register at each position. Nothing in the base
994:  evaluates a numeric predicate, and that is the point: the arithmetic must be
995:  built, which `DescriptiveComplexity.leSweep_accepts` and
996:  `DescriptiveComplexity.plusSweep_accepts` do for `≤` and `plus` – the
997:  bit-level analogues of `DescriptiveComplexity.HeadProgram.plusP`. The model is
998:  **exactly a logic** (`DescriptiveComplexity.ltDecidable_iff_bitDefinable`):
999:  logarithmic time with constantly many alternations decides exactly the
1000:  problems defined by a *prenex* sentence over `≤`, `+` and the bit atom
1001:  `DescriptiveComplexity.BitIx` – the classical `BIT(x, i)`, the position named
1002:  by the element whose *rank* is the exponent – that is, exactly `FO(≤, BIT)`,
1003:  since `+` is itself derived (`DescriptiveComplexity.bitDef_plus_free`, by
1004:  carry-lookahead). The alternations are constant because a machine fixes its
1005:  register list and their polarities, so the class is the logarithmic-time
1006:  hierarchy `⋃ₖ Σₖ-TIME(log n)`, which is AC⁰, and not the strictly larger
1007:  ALOGTIME, i.e., DLOGTIME-uniform NC¹ ([Ruzzo 1981][ruzzo1981uniform]).
1008:  One direction (`DescriptiveComplexity.BitDefinable.ltDecidable`) compiles the
1009:  logic atom by atom; the other
1010:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.LTDecidable.bitDefinable`) is the
1011:  interesting one: a sweep carries a constant number of state bits past each of
1012:  the `log n` positions, so its whole history is a constant number of *bit
1013:  vectors over the positions*, and such a vector **is** an element of the
1014:  universe – the sentence guesses those elements and pins them with the
1015:  transition, determinism making the guess unique. The identification of that
1016:  logic with `FO(≤, +, ×)`, i.e., with `DescriptiveComplexity.AC0Definable`, is
1017:  Immerman's Thm 1.17 and is an **equality here too**
1018:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ac0Definable_iff_ltDecidable`): **the machine model is
1019:  exactly AC⁰**. One half is `DescriptiveComplexity.LTDecidable.ac0Definable`,
1020:  through `DescriptiveComplexity.powArithDef` – the definability of `i ↦ 2 ^ i`
1021:  (Thm 1.17(2)), proved by guessing two elements, the doubling chain of the
1022:  exponent below its top and that chain's own exponents packed into the fields
1023:  it delimits (`DescriptiveComplexity.powCert_iff`). The other is translated
1024:  formula by formula in `DescriptiveComplexity.LogTime.Translate` and turns on a
1025:  single atom, `DescriptiveComplexity.timesBitDef` – the bit-definability of
1026:  `orank x * orank y = orank z`, which is Thm 1.17(1) whole, built in
1027:  `DescriptiveComplexity.LogTime.BitSum` where the textbook says “exercise”.
1028:  Its floor is the **Bit Sum Lemma** (`DescriptiveComplexity.BitSum.PopAll`):
1029:  counting the ones of a word as long as the tape, by three nested packings
1030:  where the textbook sketches two – running sums co-located in the blocks they
1031:  count (`DescriptiveComplexity.BitSum.SumOk`, one construction instantiated at
1032:  two sizes), based on a guessed **table indexed by the value** of a doubly
1033:  logarithmic word, pinned by clearing one bit at a time
1034:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.BitSum.TableOk`). On top of it, the schoolbook
1035:  columns (`DescriptiveComplexity.BitSum.timesCert_iff`): each column counted
1036:  by the Bit Sum Lemma on a sub-mask of a factor, the columns cut into blocks
1037:  at a gap `g` with `2 ^ g > log n`, the weighted sum of one block certified by
1038:  a **guessed carry chain** – the remainders of the column-by-column addition,
1039:  one field per column, packed into a single element and walked with the
1040:  boundary-set-and-counter device (`DescriptiveComplexity.BitSum.RangeSum`);
1041:  the block sums of each parity then tile one element exactly, and two
1042:  additions reassemble the product. Guessing a chain per block is what breaks
1043:  the iterated-sum barrier: for the whole product the carries would be
1044:  `log n · log log n` bits, one element too few, while a block's are
1045:  `(log log n)²` – and soundness holds for *whatever* is guessed, all the size
1046:  arithmetic being paid in the completeness half and the size threshold
1047:  absorbed by `DescriptiveComplexity.BitDef.of_large`. Neither equality is
1048:  what places the model:
1049:  `DescriptiveComplexity.LTDecidable.mem_LOGSPACE` puts it inside LOGSPACE
1050:  outright, by evaluating the bit logic with a deterministic multi-head automaton
1051:  of `2 * vars + 8` heads whose bit atom is the halving loop
1052:  `DescriptiveComplexity.HeadProgram.bitP`
1053:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.HeadBit`, `DescriptiveComplexity.HeadEvalBit`). The
1054:  naming of positions is what decides this: with the *place-value* naming
1055:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.BitAt`, `DescriptiveComplexity.IsPos`, which is what
1056:  makes a bit first-order in `FO(≤, +, ×)`) every atom would be a regular
1057:  relation of the registers' bit tracks, alternation would be projection, and
1058:  the model would collapse to what a finite automaton reading the size of the
1059:  universe in binary can decide – too weak for AC⁰, which decides for instance
1060:  whether that size is prime. Reading a bit at a *guessed index* is what escapes
1061:  that, and it is what a random-access machine does.
1062:
1063:## Polynomial space, by second-order transitive closure
1064:
1065:* `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrderTransitiveClosure` – **SO(TC)**, the logic
1066:  that captures polynomial space on ordered structures ([Immerman
1067:  1999][immerman1999descriptive], ch. 10): a transitive closure taken not over
1068:  tuples of *elements*, as in `DescriptiveComplexity.TransitiveClosure`, but over
1069:  assignments of a block of *relation* variables. A
1070:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SOTCSpec` bundles the block, a transition sentence over
1071:  two copies of it – the current state and the next – and two endpoint
1072:  sentences; reachability itself is `Relation.ReflTransGen`, so no fixpoint
1073:  syntax, positivity condition or stage machinery is needed, exactly as for
1074:  SO-Horn and SO-Krom. A state is `2^(n^a)` bits remembered along a walk of
1075:  possibly exponentially many first-order steps, which is what PSPACE measures.
1076:  No modes or element tuples ride alongside the state: a relation variable of
1077:  arity `0` is a bit and one of arity `1` holding a singleton is an element
1078:  register, so a block already carries whatever finite control a walk needs.
1079:  Note that no fragment of *plain* second-order logic could play this role –
1080:  SO is PH, so such a fragment would collapse the hierarchy; an iteration
1081:  operator is unavoidable.
1082:* `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrderTransitiveClosurePull` – **SO(TC)
1083:  definability is closed under (ordered) FO reductions**
1084:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.SOTCDefinable.of_orderedReduction`). Since a state is an
1085:  assignment, the pullback is entirely the block pullback of
1086:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrderPull`: the states of the pulled walk are the
1087:  states of the original walk on the interpreted structure
1088:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.SOBlock.pullAssignEquiv`), and each sentence is pulled
1089:  back through the interpretation extended with the order and along the block –
1090:  twice for the transition sentence.
1091:* `DescriptiveComplexity.PSpace` – **the class PSPACE**
1092:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.PSPACE`), a `DescriptiveComplexity.ComplexityClass` by that
1093:  closure, with the complement operator `DescriptiveComplexity.coPSPACE` and the
1094:  hardness discharge `DescriptiveComplexity.PSPACE_hard_of_sotcDefinable`. What is
1095:  immediate is `DescriptiveComplexity.NP_subset_PSPACE`: an existential block is
1096:  the walk that guesses its state and takes no step. Two things are *not* free –
1097:  `PSPACE = coPSPACE`, since the complement of a walk is not a walk, and
1098:  `PH ⊆ PSPACE`, since a `Σₖ` sentence is not a walk either – and both are proved
1099:  downstream, in the two files below.
1100:* `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrderTransitiveClosureFree` – **SO(TC) needs no
1101:  order** (`DescriptiveComplexity.sotcDefinable_iff_free`,
1102:  `DescriptiveComplexity.mem_PSPACE_iff_sotcDefinableFree`). Unlike the clausal
1103:  fragments and the reachability logics, this one can *guess* its order, for the
1104:  reason Fagin's theorem can: a state of the walk is an assignment of relation
1105:  variables, so one more binary variable holds a candidate order, the source
1106:  condition checks that it is linear (`DescriptiveComplexity.linearGuard`,
1107:  shared with the order elimination of
1108:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrderOrdered`), every step freezes it, and the
1109:  three sentences read it in place of the order symbol. The order is then a
1110:  component of the certificate and nothing outside the specification sees it, so
1111:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SOTCDefinableFree` – definability by a
1112:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SOTCSpecFree`, stated on structures carrying **no
1113:  order at all** – defines the same class. A deterministic fragment cannot do
1114:  this, which is why `DescriptiveComplexity.PTIME`,
1115:  `DescriptiveComplexity.NL` and `DescriptiveComplexity.LOGSPACE` keep the
1116:  hypothesis.
1117:* `DescriptiveComplexity.FixedPointPartialSpace` – **FO(≤, PFP) ⊆ PSPACE**
1118:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.PFPDefinable.sotcDefinable`): a partial fixed-point
1119:  iteration *is* a deterministic walk on the assignments of its own block, so
1120:  it translates into an `DescriptiveComplexity.SOTCSpec` verbatim – source the
1121:  empty assignment, step «the next copy is one application of the step
1122:  formulas», target «a stable stage satisfying the output». No divergence
1123:  detection is needed: under the convergence-requiring semantics a diverging
1124:  iteration simply reaches no target state.
1125:* `DescriptiveComplexity.FixedPointParam` – **an element, quantified in front
1126:  of a fixed point** (`DescriptiveComplexity.mem_PTIME_exElement`): if a problem
1127:  over the vocabulary extended by a mark is FO(≤, IFP) definable, so is “some
1128:  element, marked, makes it hold”. A fixed point cannot be restarted once per
1129:  element, so the construction runs all of them at once – every relation
1130:  variable gains the parameter as a further argument, and the atom `old t`
1131:  becomes `t = parameter`. It is the deterministic counterpart of
1132:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SOTCDefinable.exBlock`, which prefixes a *walk* with a
1133:  guessed relation: a walk may guess, a fixed point may not, and one element is
1134:  what it can afford instead.
1135:* `DescriptiveComplexity.FixedPointStepRel` – **membership closure under
1136:  relativized ordered reductions** `≤ʳᶠᵒ[≤]`, which no definability notion of
1137:  the library had needed before
1138:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.IFPDefinable.of_relOrderedReduction`,
1139:  `DescriptiveComplexity.PFPDefinable.of_relOrderedReduction`): the block is
1140:  pulled back onto the definable domain with the step formulas gated by the
1141:  domain formulas of their arguments, and the assignment transfer is a
1142:  *bijection* onto the in-domain assignments – which is what a deterministic
1143:  iteration needs where an existential block would settle for less. Required
1144:  because all the library's hardness travels along relativized reductions, and
1145:  the PSPACE capture below crosses one in the membership direction.
1146:* `DescriptiveComplexity.FixedPointPartialMachine` – **PSPACE ⊆ FO(≤, PFP)**,
1147:  completing the capture theorem **FO(≤, PFP) = PSPACE**
1148:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.pfpDefinable_iff_mem_PSPACE`,
1149:  [Abiteboul–Vianu 1989][abiteboul1989fixpoint]): a partial fixed point
1150:  iterates the PSPACE-complete deterministic machine problem – load the
1151:  initial configuration from the empty assignment, take the unique machine
1152:  step while one exists, stutter on accepting or stuck configurations so that
1153:  a halting run is exactly a converging iteration – and every PSPACE problem
1154:  pulls that definition back along its relativized reduction to the machine
1155:  problem.
1156:* `DescriptiveComplexity.AbiteboulVianuOrdered` – **Abiteboul–Vianu, the
1157:  ordered case**
1158:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ifpDefinable_eq_pfpDefinable_iff_ptime_eq_pspace`):
1159:  on ordered structures the inflationary and partial fixed-point logics agree
1160:  exactly when `PTIME = PSPACE` – a corollary of the two capture theorems.
1161:* `DescriptiveComplexity.AbiteboulVianu` – **the Abiteboul–Vianu theorem**
1162:  ([Abiteboul–Vianu 1991][abiteboul1991generic];
1163:  [Ebbinghaus–Flum 1995][ebbinghaus1995finite], ch. 7): the inflationary and
1164:  partial fixed-point logics have the same expressive power **on unordered
1165:  finite structures** exactly when `PTIME = PSPACE`
1166:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ifpDefinableFree_eq_pfpDefinableFree_iff_ptime_eq_pspace`).
1167:  Right to left through the order-relativization transfer and the two
1168:  captures; left to right through the invariant structure: an order-free
1169:  FO(PFP) computation is `≡ᵏ`-invariant, so it runs on `Iᵏ A`, where
1170:  `PTIME = PSPACE` turns it into an ordered inflationary induction, pulled
1171:  back along the quotient map and stratified over the canonical order's own
1172:  induction. Stated for IFP versus PFP, as in the original – Gurevich–Shelah
1173:  is deliberately not involved.
1174:* `DescriptiveComplexity.PSpaceCompl` – **`PSPACE = coPSPACE`**
1175:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.PSPACE_eq_coPSPACE`), the first of those two, proved
1176:  downstream once QSAT is available: every SO(TC) definable problem reduces to
1177:  QSAT (through SUCCINCT-REACH and Savitch's recursive doubling), complementing
1178:  an ordered reduction is free, and the walk that decides QSAT is
1179:  *deterministic* – it computes the value of the formula rather than searching
1180:  for a witness – so reading its answer the other way round decides the
1181:  complement (`DescriptiveComplexity.qsatCompl_sotcDefinable`). That is the
1182:  logical shadow of the machine-theoretic reason: space-bounded computation can
1183:  be made deterministic, and a deterministic decider is complemented by flipping
1184:  its answer.
1185:* `DescriptiveComplexity.PSpaceHierarchy` – **`PH ⊆ PSPACE`**
1186:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.PH_subset_PSPACE`), the other one, by alternating that
1187:  complement with the second closure property of SO(TC): a walk can *guess a
1188:  block into its own state and never touch it again*
1189:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.SOTCDefinable.exBlock`), so `∃R̄` in front of an SO(TC)
1190:  condition is again one. The state of the guessing walk is an assignment of the
1191:  merged block, and its transition sentence adds one universally quantified
1192:  equivalence per relation variable of the guessed block, saying that component
1193:  is unchanged; a whole walk therefore keeps it fixed, which is what makes
1194:  accepting mean “the inner walk accepts under some assignment of it”. Peeling
1195:  the quantifier prefix one block at a time, existential blocks by that closure
1196:  and universal ones by complementing twice around it, gives every `Σₖ` and every
1197:  `Πₖ` level (`DescriptiveComplexity.sigmaP_subset_PSPACE`,
1198:  `DescriptiveComplexity.piP_subset_PSPACE`).
1199:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Problems.Machine.Space` – **the machines of the class,
1200:  membership half**: the same Turing machines that give NP and PTIME their
1201:  bridges, with the step bound simply dropped
1202:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.NTMAcceptSpace`,
1203:  `DescriptiveComplexity.DTMAcceptSpace`). A run may then be arbitrarily long,
1204:  but it never leaves the positions of the instance, so a configuration is an
1205:  assignment of a three-variable block – the tape a binary relation, the state
1206:  and the head unary marks – one step is a first-order condition on two
1207:  consecutive assignments, and acceptance is their transitive closure. That is
1208:  an SO(TC) specification, so both problems are in PSPACE
1209:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ntmAcceptSpace_mem_PSPACE`,
1210:  `DescriptiveComplexity.dtmAcceptSpace_mem_PSPACE`), hence both reduce to QSAT
1211:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ntmAcceptSpace_reduces_to_qsat`) – the machine-side
1212:  reading of Savitch's theorem. Hardness is proved once, for the *deterministic*
1213:  problem, by a machine that evaluates a quantified Boolean formula by the
1214:  standard iterative algorithm – the recursion stack being one bit per variable,
1215:  in the variable's own cell – and travels to the nondeterministic problem along
1216:  a reduction that enforces determinism as a first-order promise. So both are
1217:  PSPACE-complete (`DescriptiveComplexity.dtmAcceptSpace_PSPACE_complete`,
1218:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ntmAcceptSpace_PSPACE_complete`), which is this
1219:  framework's `PSPACE = NPSPACE`: nothing simulates a nondeterministic machine
1220:  deterministically, Savitch having already been spent logically in
1221:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Problems.Qsat`.
1222:

 succeeded in 7196ms:
1223:## The exponential classes, by expansion
1224:
1225:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential` – **EXPTIME, NEXPTIME and EXPSPACE**,
1226:  obtained by reading the polynomial-level logics over a universe one
1227:  exponential larger. An `DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion` maps a finite
1228:  ordered structure `A` to a structure whose universe is a *definable set of
1229:  tagged assignments of a second-order block* – `2^(n^a)` points on a universe
1230:  of size `n` – each relation being defined by a first-order sentence over the
1231:  base vocabulary expanded by one copy of the block per argument. This is the
1232:  same construction the library already carries for SUCCINCT-REACH, made into
1233:  data and applied to an arbitrary vocabulary; it is also the standard
1234:  type-lowering translation of higher-order logic into many-sorted first-order
1235:  logic over the power type ([Henkin 1950][henkin1950completeness]), which is
1236:  why a *second*-order fixed point over `A` is an ordinary first-order fixed
1237:  point over the expansion, and why no third-order syntax is introduced.
1238:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential.Pull` – **an interpretation followed by an
1239:  expansion is an expansion**
1240:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion.pullOrdered`), which is what makes the
1241:  notion closed under (ordered) FO reductions. Everything it needs is already
1242:  in the library: the order of an interpreted universe is definable
1243:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.FOInterpretation.ordExtend`), a block pulls back
1244:  through an interpretation (`DescriptiveComplexity.SOBlock.pull`), and
1245:  replication commutes with that pullback definitionally
1246:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.SOBlock.homAssign_replicatePullHom`) – so the
1247:  defining sentences of the composite are the pulled ones read through a
1248:  renaming of relation variables and nothing more.
1249:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential.Class` – the operator
1250:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ComplexityClass.exp`, applied to an **abstract**
1251:  class. That abstraction is the whole design: the succinctness upgrade
1252:  ([Galperin–Wigderson 1983][galperin1983succinct];
1253:  [Papadimitriou–Yannakakis 1986][papadimitriou1986note]; in general form
1254:  [Veith 1998][veith1998succinct]) is proved once, as
1255:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ComplexityClass.exp_compl` and
1256:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ComplexityClass.exp_mono`, and every exponential-level
1257:  statement is read off from its polynomial-level counterpart.
1258:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential.Classes` – the three classes.
1259:  `EXPTIME` is *defined* as SO(≤, LFP) and `EXPSPACE` as SO(≤, PFP)
1260:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.SOLFPDefinable`,
1261:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SOPFPDefinable`), and each equals the exponential of
1262:  its polynomial counterpart by theorem
1263:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.EXPTIME_eq_PTIME_exp`,
1264:  `DescriptiveComplexity.EXPSPACE_eq_PSPACE_exp`) – these are the library's own
1265:  capture theorems FO(≤, LFP) = PTIME and FO(≤, PFP) = PSPACE, read on the
1266:  expanded universe. Naming the classes after these logics follows
1267:  [Abiteboul–Vardi–Vianu 1997][abiteboul1997fixpoint], cited for the *names*
1268:  only: that work is stated in the relational, order-free setting, and here the
1269:  logics are definitions, so no capture theorem is claimed. `NEXPTIME` is
1270:  defined as `NP.exp`; its literature characterization is existential
1271:  *third*-order logic ([Leivant 1989][leivant1989descriptive];
1272:  [Hella–Turull-Torres 2006][hella2006higher]) and the library does not state
1273:  that equivalence, having no third-order syntax – an honest and narrow gap,
1274:  since NEXPTIME still gets its logical reading, guess a relation over the
1275:  expanded universe and check a first-order condition there. It gets a second
1276:  one, in a first-order syntax, from
1277:  `DescriptiveComplexity.mem_NEXPTIME_iff_sigmaSONewExpDefinable`: `∃SO[new,
1278:  exp]`, existential second-order logic that may invent exponentially many new
1279:  values.
1280:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential.Inclusions` – **`EXPTIME = coEXPTIME`**
1281:  and **`EXPSPACE = coEXPSPACE`**, inherited from
1282:  `DescriptiveComplexity.piP_zero_eq` (Grädel's capture theorem at level 0) and
1283:  `DescriptiveComplexity.PSPACE_eq_coPSPACE` (Savitch) through `exp_compl`.
1284:  Read on the definitions they say that SO(LFP) and SO(PFP) are closed under
1285:  complement. Nothing of those two developments is spent twice; no claim is
1286:  made for NEXPTIME. The inclusions `PSPACE ⊆ EXPTIME ⊆ NEXPTIME ⊆ EXPSPACE`
1287:  follow, all but the first by `exp_mono` on a polynomial-level inclusion.
1288:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential.Reach` – the one inclusion with content,
1289:  `DescriptiveComplexity.PSPACE_subset_EXPTIME`: an
1290:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SOTCSpec` *is* the graph REACH reads on the expansion
1291:  whose points are its states, the two definitions being the same sentence up
1292:  to the name of the universe. Since REACH is in every class from NL up, this
1293:  gives `PSPACE ⊆ NL.exp` as well, and `NL.exp ⊆ EXPTIME` comes back by
1294:  monotonicity. On the definitions the inclusion is **SO(TC) ⊆ SO(LFP)**, the
1295:  second-order shadow of `NL ⊆ PTIME`.
1296:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential.Game` – the same construction one operator
1297:  up, and the way into EXPTIME that needs no succinctness argument. A
1298:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SOGameSpec` is four first-order sentences over a
1299:  second-order block – which assignments the universal player owns, which win
1300:  outright, which start the game, which moves are legal, the move sentence
1301:  seeing two copies as an `DescriptiveComplexity.SOTCSpec`'s transition does –
1302:  and it *is* the AND/OR graph `DescriptiveComplexity.GAME` reads on the
1303:  expansion whose points are its states
1304:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.SOGameSpec.gameWon_toExp_iff`). Since GAME is in
1305:  PTIME, `DescriptiveComplexity.SOGameDefinable.mem_EXPTIME` follows: **SO-GAME
1306:  ⊆ SO(LFP)**, the second-order shadow of `GAME ∈ PTIME`, exactly as the
1307:  previous entry is the shadow of `REACH ∈ PTIME`. It is what an alternating
1308:  space-bounded machine consumes, its configurations being the assignments of a
1309:  block with one variable for the state, one for the head and one for the tape
1310:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.atmAcceptSpace_soGameDefinable`).
1311:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential.GameExp` – the converse, and with it
1312:  **`EXPTIME = SO-GAME`** (`DescriptiveComplexity.exptime_eq_soGame`): *the
1313:  deterministic exponential class is second-order alternating reachability*.
1314:  This is Chandra–Kozen–Stockmeyer ([Chandra–Kozen–Stockmeyer
1315:  1981][chandra1981alternation]) with the machine removed. A problem of
1316:  `SO(≤, LFP)` is a `PTIME` property of an expansion
1317:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.solfpDefinable_iff_expDefinable`), hence `GameWon` of
1318:  the AND/OR graph an interpretation draws *on the expanded universe*
1319:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.game_hard_ordered`); its four defining relations are
1320:  first-order there, so by the translation lemma they are alternating block
1321:  prefixes over the base – and a prefix is a sequence of **moves**, which is
1322:  precisely what the obstruction of `Exponential.Translate` does not forbid.
1323:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion.graphGame` plays that graph, in six
1324:  phases: the four node phases (`main`, `exStep`, `allCert`, `allStep`) and the
1325:  prefix phases that decide the six questions
1326:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.Sub`) about one or two nodes. Two conventions are what
1327:  makes the game match the logic: a leaf whose kernel fails is existential and
1328:  moveless, so an unprovable claim loses; and `allCert` certifies a successor
1329:  *before* the universal player chooses one, since
1330:  `DescriptiveComplexity.WinsOn.all` makes a stuck universal node lose.
1331:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential.Translate` – **the translation lemma**
1332:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion.exists_translate`): a first-order
1333:  sentence *over an expansion* is a second-order sentence over the base, since
1334:  a quantifier ranging over the points of the expanded universe ranges over
1335:  block assignments. This is the type-lowering reading of [Henkin
1336:  1950][henkin1950completeness] made into a theorem, and the honest statement
1337:  of the obstruction that keeps an interpretation from being composed *after*
1338:  an expansion. A quantified point is a block extended by tag bits, guarded to
1339:  satisfy its tag's domain sentence; each quantifier peels into two blocks, one
1340:  `∃` and one `∀`, of which one is real and the other vacuous, so that the
1341:  prefix alternates strictly; and the induction runs on the
1342:  `FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.IsPrenex` proof, `∃` being encoded as
1343:  `∼(∼φ).all` and so unreachable by a structural recursion.
1344:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential.Increment` – the **successor of an
1345:  assignment**, as a first-order sentence over the base and two copies of the
1346:  block: an assignment is a binary number, so the successor is the increment.
1347:  The subtlety it settles is that `DescriptiveComplexity.SOBlock.atomSet` reads
1348:  an assignment as a set of *padded* atoms, whose image is only the
1349:  padding-invariant sets, so the increment has to be taken at the honest atoms
1350:  `Σ i, Fin (B.arity i) → A` and matched to the padded order through least
1351:  representatives. With
1352:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion.trivialize` – which trades an expansion's
1353:  domain sentence for a mark, carrying an FO(TC) walk along
1354:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion.accepts_relSpec`), so that a point is
1355:  *every* tagged assignment – these are the order primitives a machine needs to
1356:  walk an expanded universe.
1357:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential.PSpaceOn` – its payoff,
1358:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion.mem_PSPACE_of_fo_on_expansion`: **every
1359:  first-order property of an exponential expansion is in `PH`, hence in
1360:  `PSPACE`**. This is one bound on the operator *from above*; most of what is
1361:  proved about it validates it from below, `PSPACE ⊆ NL.exp ⊆ EXPTIME`.
1362:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential.Simulate` – **a machine that walks an
1363:  expanded universe is a walk over the base**
1364:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion.autoSpec`,
1365:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion.accepts_autoSpec`). A configuration of a
1366:  two-way `k`-head automaton over an expansion is a control state and `k`
1367:  points, i.e., one assignment of the block
1368:  `(repMerged X.pointBlock k).withTag M.State` – a state of an
1369:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SOTCSpec`. The automaton's tests are quantifier-free
1370:  *by fiat* (`DescriptiveComplexity.HeadAutomaton.test_qf`), so
1371:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion.translQF` translates them as they stand
1372:  and no quantifier over the expanded universe is ever evaluated; its moves are
1373:  the order primitives of `Exponential.Increment`, read at a
1374:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion.PtSlot` – one interface for “a point sits
1375:  here inside that block”, used both for one configuration and for the two a
1376:  transition sentence compares. The correctness is a one-step bisimulation, the
1377:  one hypothesis being that every tagged assignment is a point, which is what
1378:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion.trivialize` arranges.
1379:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential.Gate` – **`PSPACE = NL.exp`**
1380:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.PSPACE_eq_NL_exp`): polynomial space *is*
1381:  nondeterministic logarithmic space read one exponential up. Both inclusions
1382:  are theorems, so the exponential operator is pinned at the one level where
1383:  this library independently knows the answer, and not merely bounded. The
1384:  converse half chains three constructions – carry the walk to the trivialized
1385:  expansion, compile it into an automaton
1386:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.tcDefinable_iff_automaton`), simulate the automaton.
1387:  `LOGSPACE.exp ⊆ PSPACE` follows by monotonicity; the reverse inclusion is not
1388:  claimed, REACH not being known here to be in
1389:  `DescriptiveComplexity.LOGSPACE`.
1390:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Exponential.Free`, `.FreeCopy`, `.FreeSpace`,
1391:  `.FreeTime` – **the exponential classes need no order**
1392:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.mem_EXPTIME_iff_solfpDefinableFree`,
1393:  `DescriptiveComplexity.mem_EXPSPACE_iff_sopfpDefinableFree`): the expansion's
1394:  own sentences can be written over the bare vocabulary, so that the
1395:  equivalence is asked of structures carrying no order at all, which is the
1396:  setting of [Abiteboul–Vardi–Vianu 1997][abiteboul1997fixpoint]. The order is
1397:  *guessed* into the block, exactly as
1398:  `DescriptiveComplexity.sotcDefinable_iff_free` guesses it into the state of a
1399:  walk – but the price is different: the expanded universe becomes the disjoint
1400:  union, over the linear orders of the instance, of copies of the intended one,
1401:  and the inner problem must be replaced by “**some copy answers yes**”, which
1402:  is correct precisely because the problem is order-invariant. How that
1403:  existential is paid for is what separates the two classes. `PSPACE` **guesses
1404:  the copy** as a relation and freezes it in the state of a walk
1405:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion.someCls`, on
1406:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SOTCDefinable.exBlock`, with the first-order guard that
1407:  it *is* a copy conjoined by
1408:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SOTCDefinable.and_sentence`). `PTIME` cannot guess, so
1409:  it **names the copy by one of its points**
1410:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.ExpExpansion.somePtCls`) and quantifies that point
1411:  away by carrying it through every relation variable of the induction
1412:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.mem_PTIME_exElement`). Both then read the problem
1413:  inside the copy by a relativized ordered reduction. A nullary symbol has no
1414:  copy of the block to read the guessed order from, so its content moves to a
1415:  **unary shift** whose argument names the copy – which is what lets the
1416:  construction carry no hypothesis on the arities.
1417:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Problems.Wide` – the **wide machine**, the catalog
1418:  side of the same construction and the complete problem NEXPTIME and EXPSPACE
1419:  have. Its control – transitions, states, symbols – is an ordinary
1420:  part of the instance, while its tape is addressed by the **subsets** of the
1421:  instance, so an instance of size `n` describes a machine with `2^n` cells and
1422:  `2^n` steps and the two resource variants land one exponential above
1423:  `DescriptiveComplexity.NTMAccept` and
1424:  `DescriptiveComplexity.NTMAcceptSpace`
1425:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.wideAccept_mem_NEXPTIME`,
1426:  `DescriptiveComplexity.wideAcceptSpace_mem_EXPSPACE`). Nothing is said about
1427:  resources: the machine's universe *is* the universe of an exponential
1428:  expansion whose expanded vocabulary is `FirstOrder.Language.turing` – two
1429:  tags, one for the addresses and one, cut out by a singleton domain sentence,
1430:  for the elements – so the memberships are `ExpDefinable` applied to the
1431:  polynomial-level machine problems, an expansion *after* a problem and not the
1432:  composition that does not exist. Why this and not more alternation:
1433:  with polynomially many cells an ordinary machine problem tops out at PSPACE
1434:  and an alternating one at EXPTIME whatever the play length, so the
1435:  exponentially large index set has to appear in the target problem's own
1436:  semantics. The order on addresses is the binary-number order induced by the
1437:  instance's own order, since a decision problem may not read the ambient one,
1438:  and the promises that order carries reduce to three first-order conditions
1439:  about the instance (`DescriptiveComplexity.wideData_wellFormed_iff`).
1440:  Hardness **is** proved for the space variant:
1441:  `DescriptiveComplexity.dwideAcceptSpace_EXPSPACE_complete` and
1442:  `DescriptiveComplexity.wideAcceptSpace_EXPSPACE_complete`. The program is a
1443:  roaming machine with a register file, iterating a partial fixed point over the
1444:  expansion until it stabilises – no clock, and a diverging fixed point diverges,
1445:  which is a correct *no*. Three things make it fit in a first-order
1446:  interpretation. Every rule of the emitted machine is written down by **one
1447:  formula for every instance**
1448:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.Draw.Data.uRulesDefinable_progOf`), which is what an
1449:  interpretation needs and what the guard interface
1450:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.Draw.UGDefinable`) is shaped for. The eleven relations
1451:  are read off those (`DescriptiveComplexity.Draw.Data.reads_progFrom`), the
1452:  input channel's mark being a register file whose two extremes are tag decisions
1453:  rather than quantifiers. And the base is not the instance but a **doubled**
1454:  universe (`DescriptiveComplexity.Draw.dblInterp`), which is never a singleton –
1455:  a track is an element, so the machine needs two of them, and a reduction must
1456:  be correct at one-element structures too. The price of the doubling is paid on
1457:  the expansion's side, by relativizing it to the marked half
1458:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.Draw.relExp`,
1459:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Draw.relExpMapEquiv`), and the doubling being a plain
1460:  one-dimensional interpretation the composite keeps the dimension and only
1461:  multiplies the tags by `Bool ^ dd`. Hardness for the nondeterministic variant
1462:  is the deterministic one carried along
1463:  `DescriptiveComplexity.dwideAcceptSpace_fo_reduction_wideAcceptSpace`, which is
1464:  the library's standing rule that the deterministic side is the one to prove.
1465:
1466:  **Hardness for NEXPTIME is proved too**
1467:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.wideRegAccept_NEXPTIME_complete`), at the same drawing
1468:  read one resource across: `DescriptiveComplexity.WideRegAccept` is acceptance
1469:  by a wide machine **within its clock**, `2 ^ |Univ|` steps, its tape handed to
1470:  it by the input channel rather than laid by a sweep of its own. That last
1471:  point is what the time bound forces: a clocked machine cannot afford to write
1472:  its own register file, and no wide machine can lay one anyway – laying it
1473:  needs an injective map from the tuple coordinates into the control
1474:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.Draw.not_injective_ctl_name`), which the control has
1475:  no room for. So the file arrives as a *register channel*, one cell per element
1476:  the program marks, and the program is the same clocked one with its
1477:  file-laying sweep replaced by a sweep that lays nothing
1478:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.Draw.Data.nexProgHanded`). Its run is proved both
1479:  ways: a guess making the kernel true is run into the accepting phase on the
1480:  clock, and an accepting run is *read backwards* – the tape of any reachable
1481:  configuration is recognized as the machine's own tape state
1482:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.Draw.Data.exists_entry_state`), the assignment the
1483:  guess left is read off its stage tracks
1484:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.Draw.assignOfTrack`), and the machine is deterministic
1485:  after the guess, so a false verdict cannot stand beside an accepting run. The
1486:  clock's arithmetic comes down to one inequality between the drawing's rule
1487:  names and a constant of the kernel, and a reduction meets it by giving its
1488:  program that many rules that never fire
1489:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.Draw.Data.nexProgHandedPad`) – junk names change no
1490:  run, no separation and no constant, and every layer of the proof is stated at
1491:  whatever program provides the record
1492:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Draw.Data.NexEmitted`. The kernel is padded too, each
1493:  guessed variable gaining an argument
1494:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.NexKernel.withArg`), because a variable of arity zero
1495:  would have the empty address for its entry – the marker's own cell.
1496:
1497:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Problems.Tiling` and
1498:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Problems.Wide.Tiling` – the **tiling** ([Fürer
1499:  1983][furer1983domino]), the same construction with the machine replaced by a
1500:  drawing. A tile system is a set of
1501:  tiles with a horizontal and a vertical compatibility, a description of the
1502:  bottom row and an accepting mark, and the question is whether the square whose
1503:  sides are the *positions* can be tiled. Read on the instance itself that is an
1504:  `n × n` square and the problem is in NP
1505:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.tiling_mem_NP`, a `Σ₁` definition guessing the tiling
1506:  as one ternary relation); read over the address expansion the same definition
1507:  asks about a `2ⁿ × 2ⁿ` square and is NEXPTIME-complete
1508:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.wideTiling_NEXPTIME_complete`). The point of the
1509:  problem is that its conditions are *local* in two dimensions – no head, no
1510:  clock, no mirror – so it is the cheap second complete problem of a class whose
1511:  first one is a machine. Its bottom row is described at the **cells of a
1512:  file**, with a base tile where the description is silent and a start tile at
1513:  the corner, which is the same device as the register channel's input and for
1514:  the same reason: the hardness is the clocked machine drawn as a table
1515:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.Problems.Wide.TilingHard`), a row per configuration
1516:  and a column per address, so the two tapes have to be described the same way.
1517:  A tile carries the transition its head fires and an **arrival** is a tile of
1518:  its own – the handshake that keeps a row to one head with rules seeing two
1519:  cells at most – and the two **edge columns** carry marks of their own
1520:  (`ledge`, `redge`, the classical border colors): an arrival at the leftmost
1521:  column is sent by no neighbor, so without them a head would appear there out
1522:  of nowhere and a no-instance would be tileable.
1523:
1524:* `DescriptiveComplexity.CORRIDOR` and `DescriptiveComplexity.WideCorridor` –
1525:  the same tile system asked the **other** question: tiling the corridor of that
1526:  width and unbounded height. A corridor *is* a walk whose states are its rows,
1527:  so its membership is a transcription into
1528:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SOTCSpec` (`DescriptiveComplexity.corridor_mem_PSPACE`)
1529:  and, read over the address expansion, it is EXPSPACE-complete
1530:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.wideCorridor_EXPSPACE_complete`). Its hardness is the
1531:  square's drawing with the clock taken out – the rows are the configurations of
1532:  a machine bounded in *space* – and the only thing that changes is the bottom
1533:  row, the two machines describing their tapes differently: that row is
1534:  therefore a parameter of both the drawing
1535:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.TilingHard.tileStrOf`) and the interpretation that
1536:  writes it down.
1537:* `DescriptiveComplexity.EPR` – **satisfiability of an `∃*∀*` sentence**, the
1538:  Bernays–Schönfinkel–Ramsey class ([Lewis 1980][lewis1980complexity]). The
1539:  instance is the sentence itself, flat: the existential variables are marked,
1540:  the matrix is a set of clauses of literals over relation symbols of the
1541:  instance's own making, and there is no parse tree and no order – a prenex form
1542:  with a quantifier-free matrix needs neither. Satisfiability is defined on the
1543:  encoding, as for `DescriptiveComplexity.FINSAT`, a model being a universe with
1544:  a *local* interpretation of the symbols and a witness for the existential
1545:  variables. It is in NEXPTIME (`DescriptiveComplexity.epr_mem_NEXPTIME`) by the
1546:  two halves of the classical argument: the **small-model property**
1547:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.Epr.selfModel_of_eprSatOn` – collapse the model onto
1548:  the instance by sending each existential variable to its witness), and one
1549:  `Σ₁` sentence read over an expansion whose points are the *relations* on the
1550:  instance (`DescriptiveComplexity.Epr.eprExp`), an assignment of the universal
1551:  variables being one of those points. Its hardness is not formalized yet.
1552:
1553:* `DescriptiveComplexity.AddrExp` – the **address expansion**, written once for
1554:  an arbitrary relational vocabulary with a designated order symbol: the block is
1555:  one unary relation variable, so an assignment *is* a subset of the instance and
1556:  the expanded universe is its power set; two tags keep the base universe visible
1557:  inside it; and five sentences – a mark, a binary attribute, being a singleton,
1558:  the binary-number order on addresses, and a relation read at the cells of a
1559:  file – are everything a problem drawn on it has to say. Both the wide machine
1560:  and the wide tiling are `DescriptiveComplexity.AddrExp.addrExp` at their own
1561:  vocabulary, and the embedding of the problem's universe into the expansion is
1562:  proved there once.

 succeeded in 10378ms:
454:## Inexpressibility: Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé games
455:
456:The one part of the library that proves things logic *cannot* do, with no
457:complexity-theoretic assumption anywhere – the payoff a machine-first
458:development has no counterpart for.
459:
460:* `DescriptiveComplexity.FirstOrderDefinable` – plain first-order
461:  definability of a decision problem, order-free
462:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.FODefinableFree`) and order-invariant
463:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.FODefinable`), the bottom of every ladder above and
464:  the notion these results refute.
465:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Games.Ehrenfeucht` – **the Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé
466:  game** ([Ehrenfeucht 1961][ehrenfeucht1961application]) between two
467:  structures: legal positions (`DescriptiveComplexity.PartialIso`, agreement
468:  on the atomic type read across two structures), the graded refinement
469:  `DescriptiveComplexity.efStage` – whose rounds *append* a coordinate over
470:  two structures, which is why it is not an instance of the `≡ᵏ` pebble
471:  skeleton of `DescriptiveComplexity.Invariant.Pebble` – and **the
472:  methodology lemma** (`DescriptiveComplexity.realize_sentence_of_efEquiv`):
473:  `n`-round equivalent structures satisfy the same sentences of quantifier
474:  rank at most `n`, the measure being the `DescriptiveComplexity.qdepth`
475:  shared with the invariant layer. Everything below is a contrapositive of it.
476:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Games.Bare` – the strategy on **bare sets**: two
477:  sets with at least `n` elements each are `n`-round equivalent
478:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.efEquiv_bare`), so an order-free first-order
479:  definable property of a bare set is constant beyond a threshold
480:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.exists_card_bound_of_foDefinableFree`) – first-order
481:  logic counts up to its quantifier rank and no further.
482:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Games.Distance`,
483:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Games.LinearOrder` – **Ehrenfeucht's theorem on
484:  linear orders**: two finite linear orders with at least `2 ^ n` elements
485:  each are `n`-round equivalent (`DescriptiveComplexity.efEquiv_linearOrder`).
486:  The duplicator's invariant is one equation per pair of points – equal
487:  distances *up to truncation at* `2 ^ n` (`DescriptiveComplexity.truncAt`),
488:  with the two ends of the order joined to the position as sentinels so that
489:  distances to them are distances like any other – and a round is one
490:  application of the answer lemma `DescriptiveComplexity.exists_answer`, where
491:  the budget halves: copy the distance to the nearer neighbor, or, when both
492:  are far, land in the middle of a gap the invariant makes twice as wide on
493:  the other side.
494:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Invariant.Bare` – **the order no induction defines**:
495:  over the empty vocabulary `≡ᵏ` is the equality pattern
496:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.equivK_bare`, the pebble twin of
497:  `DescriptiveComplexity.efStage_bare`), so a transposition of the universe
498:  leaves it alone and every binary variable of an order-free inflationary
499:  limit is symmetric – whence
500:  `DescriptiveComplexity.not_isLinearOrder_inflLimit`: **no order-free
501:  `StepDef` defines a linear order on a bare set**. This is the
502:  order-invariance of the definability notions of this library as a theorem:
503:  the order they are handed is not a convenience but something no
504:  isomorphism-invariant logic can build. It is a statement about a defined
505:  *relation*; the class-level one needs the two-structure game below, since
506:  `≡ᵏ` relates tuples inside one structure.
507:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Invariant.TwoPebble`,
508:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Invariant.TwoInvariance`,
509:  `DescriptiveComplexity.Invariant.TwoStages` – **the `k`-pebble game between
510:  two structures**, the pebble counterpart of the round game above and the
511:  layer a *Boolean* query needs: the same chain, coinduction and stabilization
512:  with the two sides in different types (`DescriptiveComplexity.EquivK₂`), the
513:  `k`-variable invariance lemma across the pair
514:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.realize_equivK₂`), the collapse on bare sets
515:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.equivK₂_bare`: `k` pebbles cannot count past `k`,
516:  whatever the two sizes), and the transfer of an inflationary induction stage
517:  by stage (`DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef.inflStage_invariant₂`), so that its
518:  output sentence cannot separate the two structures
519:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.StepDef.ifpHolds_equivK₂`).
520:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Problems.Even` – **EVEN is not first-order
521:  definable** (`DescriptiveComplexity.even_not_foDefinableFree`), and **not
522:  even order-invariantly so** (`DescriptiveComplexity.even_not_foDefinable`):
523:  over the empty vocabulary, deciding the parity of the universe is beyond
524:  first-order logic however it is allowed to use a linear order. It is a
525:  single walk along that order, though – step to the successor, flip a bit –
526:  so it *is* FO(≤, TC) definable (`DescriptiveComplexity.even_tcDefinable`),
527:  hence in `DescriptiveComplexity.NL` (`DescriptiveComplexity.even_mem_NL`).
528:  Together with the trivial inclusion
529:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.FODefinable.tcDefinable`, in
530:  `DescriptiveComplexity.TransitiveClosureFO`: a sentence is the walk that
531:  takes no step – and a walk with no step is deterministic for want of a
532:  competitor, so the same construction gives
533:  `DescriptiveComplexity.FODefinable.dtcDefinable`, the `FO(≤) ⊆ L` end of the
534:  chain below) that is **`FO ⊊ FO(TC)`**, unconditionally
535:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.exists_tcDefinable_not_foDefinable`) – a strict
536:  inclusion proved outright, where every other separation in this library is
537:  conditional. The same problem separates the *arithmetic* logic from the bare
538:  order, in the other direction: EVEN **is** AC⁰ definable
539:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.even_ac0Definable`), the greatest element having rank
540:  `Nat.card A - 1`, whence **`FO(≤) ⊊ AC⁰`**
541:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.exists_ac0Definable_not_foDefinable`). That is the
542:  parity of the *universe*, i.e., of the input's length; the parity of a marked
543:  *subset* is PARITY, the problem outside AC⁰, about which nothing here is
544:  claimed – no AC⁰ lower bound is proved in this library. EVEN also settles the
545:  *unordered* fixed-point question:
546:  `DescriptiveComplexity.even_not_ifpDefinableFree`, whence
547:  `DescriptiveComplexity.exists_mem_PTIME_not_ifpDefinableFree` – **order-free
548:  FO(IFP) does not capture PTIME**, against
549:  `DescriptiveComplexity.lfpDefinable_iff_mem_PTIME`, which says it does over
550:  ordered structures. The order in every capture theorem here is doing real
551:  work.
552:* `DescriptiveComplexity.Problems.Parity` – **PARITY**, the parity of a *marked
553:  subset* rather than of the universe: the problem the AC⁰ lower bound is about,
554:  in the catalog so that the distinction from EVEN is a definition and not a
555:  warning. It is **in LOGSPACE** (`DescriptiveComplexity.parity_mem_LOGSPACE`) by
556:  one deterministic walk – carry a bit, flip it at each marked element, a walk
557:  functional outright so that determinizing is free – and **not first-order
558:  definable** (`DescriptiveComplexity.parity_not_foDefinable`), EVEN being the
559:  instance where everything is marked
560:  (`DescriptiveComplexity.even_fo_reduction_parity`). With
561:  `DescriptiveComplexity.even_ac0Definable` and
562:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ac0Definable_mem_PTIME` that is three sides of
563:  `AC⁰ ⊊ LOGSPACE`; the fourth, PARITY ∉ AC⁰, is the switching lemma
564:  ([Ajtai 1983][ajtai1983sigma11]; [Furst, Saxe & Sipser 1984][furst1984parity];
565:  [Håstad 1986][hastad1986almost]) and is not proved here – this library proves
566:  **no** AC⁰ lower bound.
567:
568:## Nondeterministic logarithmic space, by the Krom fragment
569:
570:* `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrderKrom` – SO-Krom ([Grädel
571:  1992][gradel1992capturing]): the same clausal style with the *Krom* (2-CNF)
572:  restriction in place of the Horn one, at most two second-order literals per
573:  clause and of either sign (`DescriptiveComplexity.KromProgram`, whose literals carry
574:  a sign and sit in two `Option` slots, so unit and goal clauses need no
575:  special case). It captures nondeterministic logarithmic space on ordered
576:  structures. Neither fragment contains the other: Horn clauses may be wide,
577:  Krom clauses may have two positive literals – and the difference is exactly
578:  determinism, a Horn program having a least model where a 2-CNF has none.
579:* `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrderKromPull` – the pullback stays Krom, for the reason
580:  it stays Horn (the shape constrains second-order atoms; an interpretation
581:  rewrites input-vocabulary ones, which live in the guard), so
582:  `DescriptiveComplexity.NL` in `DescriptiveComplexity.LogSpace` is a genuine complexity
583:  class. The pieces shared with the Horn pullback (atoms, guard pullback, tag
584:  assignments) live in `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrder` and
585:  `DescriptiveComplexity.SecondOrderPull`.
586:* `DescriptiveComplexity.LogSpace` – the class `DescriptiveComplexity.NL`. Its inclusion
587:  in the classes above is *not* syntactic (a Krom kernel is not a Horn kernel)
588:  and goes through the complete problem: `DescriptiveComplexity.NL_subset_PTIME` and
589:  `DescriptiveComplexity.NL_subset_NP`, both downstream with 2SAT. That the class is
590:  closed under complement – `NL = coNL` – is *not* the definitional duality
591:  that gives `PiP k` from `SigmaP k` but Immerman–Szelepcsényi, proved in
592:  `DescriptiveComplexity.ImmermanSzelepcsenyi` (`DescriptiveComplexity.NL_eq_coNL`).
593:* `DescriptiveComplexity.TransitiveClosure` – FO(TC) ([Immerman
594:  1987][immerman1987languages]), the logic that captures NL on ordered
595:  structures, in the same kernel-as-data style: a `DescriptiveComplexity.TCSpec` is an
596:  arity, a finite *mode* component, a first-order transition formula on
